plans.title: Fielding Focus — Station Night
plans.summary: Station-based fielding practice with warm-up competition, 3 simultaneous drill stations, team situational defense, and a hitting block to close.
plans.notes: 3 coaches running simultaneous stations. Players rotate every 10 minutes through 2 infield stations and 1 outfield station.

blocks.details: Full team on the outfield grass. Jog, high knees, butt kicks, shuffles, arm circles, torso twists, wrist/finger stretches.

drillLinks.label: Youth Baseball Practice Warm-Up Routine
5 Dynamic Stretches for Baseball Warmup

coachingPoints: Keep it controlled — this isn't a race
Big arm circles forward and backward, 10 each direction
Finish with wrist circles and finger stretches

blocks.details: Partner catch starting at 30 ft, backing up to 60 ft then 90 ft. Competition: track passed balls and errant throws per pair. Pair with fewest errors wins. Keeps reps sharp and competitive.

drillLinks.label: Youth Baseball: Simple Throwing Progressions
A Throwing Routine For All Youth Baseball Players

coachingPoints: Four-seam grip on every throw
Step toward your target — don't just arm it
Follow through: throwing hand finishes near the opposite hip
Scorekeeping: each dropped ball or throw that bounces before your partner counts as 1 point (low score wins)

blocks.activity: Station Rotation — 3 Simultaneous Stations (10 min each, rotate twice)
blocks.details:
Split players into 3 groups. Each coach runs one station. Groups rotate every 10 minutes so everyone hits all 3 stations.

📍 STATION 1 — Infield: Ground Ball Fundamentals (Coach 1)
Focus on athletic ready position, approaching the ball, and funneling with two hands. Mix in straight-on, forehand, and slow roller reps.

📍 STATION 2 — Infield: Backhand Ground Ball Drill (Coach 2)
Focus exclusively on balls to the throwing-hand side. Crossover step, glove angle (fingers down), field off the right foot, quick throw.

📍 STATION 3 — Outfield: Drop Step Fly Ball Drill (Coach 3)
Coach calls L/R or signals deep. Player drop steps, tracks ball over the shoulder, catches while moving forward. Finish with a crow hop throw back.

drillLinks.label: Station 1: How to Field a Ground Ball in 3 Easy Steps
Station 1: 3 Simple Baseball Fielding Drills for Youth Players
Station 2: How To Field a Ground Ball Backhand
Station 2: Forehand & Backhand Athleticism
Station 3: 3 Great Outfield Drills for Youth Players
Station 3: Outfield Drills You MUST Be Doing!

coachingPoints: Station 1: Field out front, funnel to the belly button, two hands when possible
Station 2: Crossover first — don't reach. Fingers DOWN on the backhand.
Station 3: Drop step immediately — no backpedaling. Call the ball every rep.
Rotate on coach's whistle. Reset and be ready before the next rep comes.

blocks.details: Full defense on the field. Coach announces the situation and hits fungoes. Place 1-2 base runners. Defense must communicate, make the correct play, and back each other up — just like a real game. Mix in cutoffs, relay reads, and force plays.

drillLinks.label: Game-Like Drills for Efficient Baseball Practice

coachingPoints: Everyone has a job on every play — no spectators
Talk before the pitch: 'Where am I going with this ball?'
Back-up responsibilities matter as much as the primary play
Reset after each play — don't carry a mistake into the next one

blocks.details: Coach pitches from flat ground or short mound. Rotate batters every 5-6 pitches. Fielders in the field making live plays on balls in play. Suggested round structure: Round 1 — hit it where it's pitched; Round 2 — opposite field focus; Round 3 — situational (runner on 3rd, less than 2 outs — get the run in).
coachingPoints: Keep the fielders engaged — they're taking reps too
Situational round: if they pull an opposite-field pitch, that's a win too — process over result
Keep the line moving, minimize standing around

blocks.activity: Position Group: 2B & SS — Double Play Work
blocks.details: 2B and SS stay after while others are dismissed. Focus exclusively on double play feeds and pivots. Coach hits ground balls to third or first; middle infielders work the feed to second and relay to first. Alternate who covers the bag.

drillLinks.label: How to Turn a Double Play — 3 Steps for Youth Players
Double Play Drills with Bill Ripken
Double Play Infield Tips and Drills (Antonelli Baseball)

coachingPoints: Get to the bag EARLY — you need to be set before the throw arrives
Inside pivot (ball from 3B side): catch, drag the bag, throw
Outside pivot (ball from 1B side): catch, step around, throw
Short, quick throw to first — no wind-up. Get rid of it.

plans.coachNotes: 3 coaches needed for station rotation (0:15-0:45). Assign your most experienced coach to Station 2 (backhand) — it needs the most technical feedback. After practice, only need 1 coach to stay for the 2B/SS optional block.

plans.title: Cutoffs, Relays & Hitting Night
plans.summary: Station-based fundamentals to open, then two focused team defense blocks on cutoffs and relay mechanics, closing with a hitting rotation. Four coaches running simultaneous stations during the fundamentals block.
plans.notes: 4 coaches for station block (0:15–0:45). Relay Race Game needs full team. Cutoff block needs 1–2 volunteer baserunners.

blocks.details: Full team on outfield grass. Jog, high knees, butt kicks, shuffles, arm circles (10 each direction forward/back), torso twists, wrist/finger stretches.

drillLinks.label: Youth Baseball Practice Warm-Up Routine
5 Dynamic Stretches for Baseball Warmup

coachingPoints: Controlled — not a race
Big arm circles, both directions
Finish with wrist and finger stretches

blocks.details: Pairs start at 30 ft, back up to 60 ft, then 90 ft. Four-seam grip, step toward target, full follow-through every rep.

drillLinks.label: Youth Baseball: Simple Throwing Progressions

coachingPoints: Four-seam grip every throw
Step toward your target — no lazy lob throws
Follow through: throwing hand finishes near opposite hip
Catch with two hands when possible

blocks.activity: Fundamental Stations — 4 Simultaneous (10 min each, rotate 3 times)
blocks.details:
Split players into 4 groups. Each coach runs one station. Groups rotate on whistle every 10 minutes. Adjust group sizes if needed — outfield station can handle larger groups.

📍 STATION 1 — Ground Ball Fundamentals (Coach 1)
Athletic ready position, approach and read, field out front. Mix straight-on, slow rollers, and short hops. Throw to a partner or bucket after each rep.

📍 STATION 2 — Throwing Mechanics (Coach 2)
Start on one knee: wrist snap and arm path only. Move to standing no-step throws, then full throws. Emphasize four-seam grip, elbow up, hip-shoulder separation, follow through.

📍 STATION 3 — Fly Ball / Drop Step (Coach 3)
Coach calls direction or signals deep. Player drop steps, tracks over the shoulder, catches moving forward. Crow hop throw back every rep. Outfielders + any overflow infielders.

📍 STATION 4 — Crow Hop & Relay Throw (Coach 4)
Player fields a rolled ball, executes crow hop, and fires a low throw to a target at 70–80 ft. Focus on the footwork pattern (catch → replace step → hop → throw) and keeping the throw chest-to-knee height.

drillLinks.label: Station 1: How to Field a Ground Ball in 3 Easy Steps
Station 2: Baseball Throwing Drills Youth Players MUST Be Doing
Station 3: Outfield Drills for Youth Players
Station 4: Crow Hop & Relay Throw Mechanics

coachingPoints: Station 1: Field out front, funnel to the belly button, soft hands
Station 2: Start on one knee — no body, just wrist snap — then build up to full throw
Station 3: Drop step FIRST, then track. No backpedaling ever.
Station 4: Crow hop pattern: catch → replace → hop → throw. Low throw, no rainbows.
Rotate on whistle. Reset and ready before the next rep.

blocks.activity: Relay Race Game — Fence to Home
blocks.details:
Competition: split into 2 teams. Ball starts at the warning track fence (or deepest outfield). Players must relay the ball home using proper cutoff positioning — no skipping the cutoff, no rainbow throws. Time each team from first touch at the fence to the ball reaching home plate. 3 rounds; fastest cumulative time wins.

Setup: each team picks its relay chain (outfielder → SS/2B relay → home). Coach or player at fence rolls/throws the starting ball. Timer starts when the outfielder touches it.

Variation: add a baserunner rounding third on the throw — now the defense has to actually cut or let it go based on where the runner is.

drillLinks.label: Cuts and Relay Drill
Little League Cuts and Relays Done Right

coachingPoints: Cutoff must be in a straight line from fence to home — they set the line, the OF throws to them
Throw LOW: a low throw gets there faster than a rainbow
Cutoff: turn to your glove side on the catch for the quickest release
If you let the ball go past the relay man, your team gets a time penalty
Competition reveals bad habits quickly — fix them between rounds, not during

blocks.activity: Cutoffs with Runner on 2nd — Overview then Live
blocks.details:
First 8–10 min: walk-through, no live baserunners. Coach hits or throws to each outfield zone while players walk to their cutoff positions. Stop and correct alignment, verbal calls, and backup assignments before going live.

Scenarios to cover:
• Single to left field, runner on 2B scoring
• Single to right field, runner on 2B scoring
• Ball in the gap (potential double), runner on 2B — double cutoff

SS takes throws from LF side; 2B takes throws from RF side.
3B or catcher makes the verbal call: 'CUT TWO!', 'CUT HOME!', or silence = relay through.

Last 15 min: live baserunners. Run through all 3 scenarios with real runners. Score: 1 pt defense if runner is held or thrown out. 1 pt offense if runner scores or advances.

drillLinks.label: Little League Cuts and Relays Done Right
How to Perform a Cut-Off Play // Youth Baseball
Pro Baseball Insider: Relay & Cutoff Fundamentals

coachingPoints: Cutoff man: get in a straight line. Move your feet until the outfielder, you, and the target base are all in a line.
Outfielder: throw through the cutoff at chest height — don't lob it over their head
Verbal caller (3B/C): commit LOUD and EARLY — hesitation kills the play
'CUT HOME!' = cut it and fire home. 'CUT TWO!' = cut and hold at second. Silence = let it go through
Runner on 2B with a single to left: SS is cutoff, catcher makes the call
Runner on 2B with a single to right: 2B is cutoff, first base coach or catcher makes the call
Everyone has a backup job — P covers home area on throws, 3B covers 3B, 1B covers 1B

blocks.activity: Hitting Block — Tee / Front Toss / Bullpen
blocks.details:
Split into 3 simultaneous stations with coaches rotating supervision. Run until 7:00.

🏏 STATION A — Tee Work (self-supervised with check-ins)
Hitters work off the tee focusing on contact point, hip rotation, and extension. 20 cuts, break, 20 more.

🏏 STATION B — Front Toss (Coach or parent volunteer)
Coach sits 15–20 ft away, tosses underhand. Hitters focus on tracking and driving the ball up the middle. 10 tosses per round, quick rotation.

🏏 BULLPEN — Mound/Live Arm Pitchers (separate area)
A handful of players who need mound time get organized bullpen reps while the hitting stations run. Catcher receives; coach observes mechanics and count situations if needed.

drillLinks.label: Tee Work: 3 Must-Do Batting Tee Drills
Front Toss: How to Throw Front Toss (Baseball Rebellion)

coachingPoints: Tee: contact point is out in front — if the ball goes foul, they're late; if it goes to opposite field weakly, they're early
Front toss: hands through the ball, not around it — punish mistakes down the middle
Bullpen: pitchers throw with intent. Don't just lob it for strikes — work your pitches.
Keep lines short and moving — standing around kills it

plans.coachNotes: 4 coaches needed for the station block (5:30–6:00). Relay Race Game can be run by 1 coach with a stopwatch. Cutoff block benefits from 1 coach as the hitter + 1 floating to correct alignment. For the hitting block, a parent volunteer at front toss frees coaches for bullpen and tee check-ins.
